Hi team — attaching the artifacts requested. Quick summary inline:

- Architecture diagram: we host inference and short-term caches in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Control plane is in a customer-specific private control plane (can be deployed in EU for Private customers). Backups: daily snapshots stored in EU-only S3 buckets with object locks disabled by default; we can enable shorter retention per contract. See attachment: redwood-eu-processing-diagram.png.

- SCCs mapping: we rely on the standard EU SCCs (2021) with our controller/processor annexes. No deviations; we add contractual supplementary safeguards for high-risk customers (e.g., contractually-enforced in-region KMS). Doc: HealthOps_SCCS_comparison.xlsx.

- Deletion flow: primary data purged within 24 hours of an operator-initiated removal for inference artifacts; backups pruned at the next snapshot cycle (configurable to 7/14/30 days per agreement). KMS logs and audit trail entries retained per our retention schedule and can be exported as evidence. Attached is a deletion-cert-template.pdf you can send to customers.

Notes / caveats:
- For Private deployments (customer-managed VPC/on-prem) we can provide full in-region proofs; for Hosted (multi-tenant) we provide controls, contractual commitments, and evidence exports, but isolated physical tenancy is not guaranteed unless Dedicated.
- If HealthOps requires in-region-only control plane, we should scope as a Private deployment (this has implications for pricing and timeline).

I uploaded the files to the Drive folder and added a short doc with timestamps for evidence extraction. Link: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/privacy/healthops/eu-processing-summary.docx

Thanks,
